All.label: Any newcomer support
All.title: A useful first-week checklist
tips: Keep your passport, immigration documents, and important account numbers in one secure place.
Ask each organization about eligibility, fees, language support, and what documents to bring.

Employment.label: Jobs and career support
Employment.title: Before you start applying
tips: Bring a resume and any work or education documents you have.
Ask about credential recognition, free job-search workshops, and interview practice.

Language.label: Language classes
Language.title: Language-learning tip
tips: Ask whether an assessment is needed before classes begin.
Check for childcare, evening classes, and online options if those would help.

Housing.label: Housing information
Housing.title: Housing search reminder
tips: Do not send money before seeing a rental and reviewing the agreement.
Keep records of payments and ask about tenant rights before signing.

Healthcare.label: Healthcare information
Healthcare.title: Getting health support
tips: Ask a service provider what health coverage or documents are needed.
For urgent medical help, call 911. For non-emergency health advice in Ontario, call 811.

Settlement.label: Settlement and community support
Settlement.title: Settling in Toronto
tips: Settlement workers can help you understand forms, services, and local programs.
Bring questions about school, health care, employment, housing, and community connections.

DriversLicence.label: Ontario driver's licence and photo ID
DriversLicence.title: Ontario driver's licence and photo ID
tips: A driver's licence is not the only Ontario photo ID option. Check which document fits your situation before visiting ServiceOntario.
Bring original identity and immigration documents, and confirm the exact requirements for your licence class before you go.

links.label: ServiceOntario: driver's licence and photo ID

Taxes.label: Taxes and tax-return information
Taxes.title: Taxes and tax returns
tips: Keep records of income, rent, tuition, and other receipts that may be useful when filing.
Free tax clinics may be available if you have a modest income and a simple tax situation.

SocialInsuranceNumber.label: Social Insurance Number (SIN)
SocialInsuranceNumber.title: Social Insurance Number (SIN)
tips: A SIN is needed to work in Canada and receive some government programs and benefits.
Keep your SIN private. Do not share it unless an organization has a legitimate legal reason to request it.
